title: Parameters, default values, and rest parameters
hook: Function parameters are not just names — defaults run when the argument is missing, rest collects leftovers into a real array, and both interact with destructuring in ways that surprise even experienced developers.

blocks.text: When you define `function f(a, b = 1, ...rest) {}`, each parameter is a **binding** in the function's scope. A **default value** expression runs only when the corresponding argument is `undefined` — not when it is `null` or `0`. A **rest parameter** (`...names`) gathers all remaining arguments into a genuine Array instance (not array-like `arguments`). Parameters are evaluated left to right; a default can reference earlier parameters in the same signature.

entries.plainDefinition: An initializer after = that runs when the argument is undefined.
A final ...identifier that collects excess arguments into an Array.
Legacy array-like object available inside non-arrow functions. Prefer rest parameters in modern code.

entries.example: Default params run in TDZ-safe order at call time.

blocks.text: Default parameters replace a lot of manual `if (x === undefined)` boilerplate and make APIs self-documenting. Rest parameters give you variadic functions without the quirks of `arguments` (not a real array, no arrow access). In production, a default that mutates a shared object literal is a subtle bug — each call must get a fresh default. Interviewers ask whether `null` triggers a default (it does not) and whether defaults are re-evaluated per call (yes).

blocks.title: undefined vs missing vs null
blocks.body: Only `undefined` (including omitting the argument) triggers the default. Passing `null` explicitly keeps null — design your API docs accordingly.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Create function scope
items.body: Each invocation creates a new lexical environment for parameters and locals.

items.title: Bind positional arguments
items.body: Arguments map to parameters in order. Extra args are ignored unless a rest parameter exists.

items.title: Apply defaults
items.body: If a parameter is undefined after binding, evaluate its default expression once for this call.

items.title: Build rest array
items.body: Remaining arguments after the last non-rest parameter copy into a new Array.

diagram.title: Call to parameter bindings

flowchart LR

  CALL --> REST[...rest = 3 4]
  P2 --> EVAL[Evaluate b default once]

blocks.body: function cfg(opts = {}) is safe. function bad(opts = { cache: [] }) shares one array unless you clone inside the body.

blocks.title: Rest must be last
blocks.body: function f(...a, b) is a SyntaxError. Rest parameters must be the final formal parameter.

interviewTakeaways: Default parameters apply when the argument is undefined, not null, not 0, not "".
Default expressions are evaluated at call time, left to right — they can reference earlier parameters.
Rest parameters produce a real Array; arguments is legacy, array-like, and absent in arrows.
60s: undefined triggers defaults. Rest collects extras. Destructuring in params works. Never use mutable object literals as defaults without cloning.
Follow-up: what happens if a default parameter references a later parameter?
commonPitfalls: Expecting null to trigger a default — only undefined does.
Using arguments in new code instead of rest — harder to compose and unavailable in arrows.
Strong answer: 'Defaults per call, undefined-only. Rest for variadics. Destructure in signature for options objects. Clone mutable defaults inside the body.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: TypeScript optional `name?: string` allows omitting the argument; combined with strictNullChecks, callers must not pass undefined unless typed explicitly.
C# params arrays are compile-time sugar for variable argument lists. JavaScript rest is always an Array at runtime with no params keyword.
